segments.text: Of the second Speciall Distresse, arisi•g from outward afflictions.

THe second kind of Distresse is that which ariseth from outward afflictions. By Afflictions I vnderstand, all manner of miseries and calamities in this life, from the least to the greatest, from the paine of the little finger, to the very pangs of death.
Nowe the Question is, howe the Trouble of minde, arising by Afflictions, may be remedied. For the answer of which question, two things are required of the partie distressed, Practise and Meditation.
